title: Audit telemetry consolidation & ship plan (wip)
content:
Purpose
This note sketch proposes a pragmatic approach to consolidate and minimize private-deploy audit telemetry (logs, approval events, and evidence bundles) so customers with customer-managed networking can: (1) get strong forensic guarantees, (2) avoid shipping huge payloads across low-bandwidth management links, and (3) keep operator UX simple for handoffs and emergency rollbacks.

Context and problem statement
- We support Private (VPC/on-prem) customers who ask for detailed audit logs and approval traces for any network/operator change, but many enterprise environments have constrained management pipes (air-gapped or periodic sync windows).
- Current product variants produce verbose telemetry: full syslog dumps, multi-step approval artifacts, and replayable snapshots. That creates heavy transfer costs, and customers have asked for configurable minimization that preserves legal/forensic fidelity.
- Goal: define a compact, verifiable telemetry model + approval gate semantics that meets security/compliance needs and is practical for export and long-term retention.

Non-goals
- This doc does not try to define end-to-end encryption schemes or replace customer KMS choices. It assumes keys/attestation live with the customer for Private deployments.
- This is not the final schema. It's a ship-plan and experiment plan for Q1–Q2.

Key design principles
1) Minimization by design: primary artifacts are small, human-readable summaries + stable compact proofs (hashes, signatures).
2) Replayable verification: allow a third-party (internal or customer auditor) to verify that a compact bundle corresponds to a full on-host snapshot without requiring full transfer in normal flow.
3) Pluggable export policies: customer can choose one of three modes — Full, Compact, and Event-only — with clear trade-offs.
4) Immutable decision records: approval-gate decisions must be cryptographically bound to evidence bundle identifiers and operator identity.

Proposed artifact types (compact model)
- activity-summary.txt (canonical text blurb, ~1–3KB): natural-language summary generated from the approval flow and operator notes.
- decision-record.json (compact JSON; typically ~2–5KB): keys: timestamp, gate-id, decision, operator-id, decision-hash. The JSON will be deliberately small and easily searchable.
- evidence-index (list of digests): ordered list of SHA256 digests referencing heavyweight artifacts (full syslog chunks, packet captures, config diffs) that remain on-device or in customer storage.
- attestation-token.sig (binary blob, base64 for export): compact signature produced by the operator device or a customer HSM signing the decision-record + evidence-index root hash.
- optional payloads (fetch-by-need): full-logs.tgz, pcap.tgz — stored encrypted locally, only transferred on-demand using a fetch protocol.

Approval gate semantics (how decision flows map to artifacts)
- Gate types: automated, operator-ack, delegated-approval, emergency-override.
- For operator-ack and delegated-approval: require creation of decision-record + activity-summary + attestation-token. The UI will require a short free-text justification field (max 300 chars) that becomes part of activity-summary.
- Emergency-override: still produces artifacts but flags high-priority tag in decision-record and places a 7-day retention/fast-ship window to encourage immediate export.

Export modes and UX tradeoffs
1) Full: export everything (default for trials). Good for initial onboarding.
2) Compact: export only the compact artifacts (activity-summary, decision-record, evidence-index, attestation-token). Full logs retained locally and fetchable. This is the recommended default for most customers.
3) Event-only: export only top-level events (decision-records); evidence-index only on request. Best for bandwidth constrained sites that keep long archives locally.
UI implications
- Console: new "Audit export" toggle on the tenant settings with per-operator override.
- Handoff: when a customer requests a handoff package, the console constructs a signed bundle (compact by default) and exposes an s3/transfer endpoint or signed URL.
- Quick-replay: add a "verify bundle" button that fetches the attestation-token and verifies against the recorded public key (supports customer or Redwood key if agreed).

Operational flows and runbook notes
- Normal flow: operator makes change -> approval gate evaluates -> compact artifacts auto-generated -> compact bundle exported according to tenant export policy.
- Forensics flow: auditor uses evidence-index to request fetches (pull model) for specific digests. Customer agent provides encrypted blobs.
- Emergency flow: emergency override triggers immediate high-priority export and alert to on-call (Slack + console).

Success criteria / metrics (experiments)
- Bandwidth reduction: median daily export size reduced by >=80% for Compact vs Full for customers with baseline >500MB/day.
- On-demand fetch latency: full artifact fetch < 90s for 95% of requests across supported regions.
- Audit completeness: external compliance tester can verify a compact bundle against local full artifacts with 100% fidelity for 100 sampled changes.
- UX: operator time to approve (with required justification) increases by < 2s median.

Risks and open questions
- Legal/compliance: Do regulators accept hash-only proofs for certain classes of change evidence? Need legal opinion.
- Key management: who holds verification keys for attestation-tokens in mixed-hosting contracts? Default to customer KMS where available.
- Retrieval scale: customer-managed storage may be slow; need prefetch strategies for common queries.
- Backcompat with existing private telemetry: migration path required.

Implementation sketch and milestones (Q1–Q2)
- Week 1–3: finalize compact artifact format (decision-record fields, canonical text rules). Produce reference generator library (Go + Python).
- Week 4–6: implement compact artifact generator on operator agent; local indexer + digest store.
- Week 7–10: console integration: export policy UI, bundle builder, preliminary verify tool.
- Week 11–14: fetch-by-need API + access-control + pre-signed URL flows; basic performance optimizations.
- Week 15–20: pilot with 2–3 existing Private customers (low-bandwidth sites) and run compliance tests.

Data model (notes for eng)
- decision-record fields (minimal): id, tenant-id, gate-id, timestamp_iso, operator_id, decision, justification_excerpt, evidence_index_root_hash, signature_b64, version. Keep version small.
- evidence-index: merkle-friendly ordered list (helps compact proofs).

Test plan
- Unit tests: canonicalization tests for activity-summary generation (same input -> same normalized output).
- Integration tests: sign/verify cycles using both Redwood test CA and a simulated customer HSM.
- E2E: simulate 1000 operator changes with mixed export policies and measure export sizes and fetch latencies.

Next steps (immediate)
- Legal ask: get preliminary legal acceptance for hash-only proofs for three named geographies (US, UK, DE). Owner: Elena.
- Engineering spike: Ravi to spike merkle-indexing approach and come back with perf numbers.
- UX: Jon to mock the export policy toggle and the bundle-verify flow for console review.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a deliberate lean approach to reduce transfer costs while preserving forensics. Feedback particularly wanted on: whether the activity-summary content is defensible for compliance reviews; acceptable signature formats; and whether emergency fast-ship semantics are sufficient.

Quick links / references
- Related tickets: ENG-1427 (evidence index prototype), SEC-621 (attestation requirements), CS-209 (customer request: low-bandwidth handoff).
- Slack thread: #private-deploy-audit (see thread pinned messages: https://slack-redwood.example/archives/C0456)

Appendix (example decision-record canonical text)
- Example snippet (canonical form):
  "At 2025-11-12T14:03:12Z, operator: r.kapoor performed tenant-edge:apply-config (change-id=chg-9f2a). Gate: delegated-approval. Decision: approved. Justification: \"rolled forward fix for dead-letter routing; verified checksums\". Evidence root: sha256:12ab...; signature: base64:MIIB...\"",
  "This example must be normalized by the reference library before signing to avoid spacing differences."
